title: Pipeline for the removal of hardware related artifacts and background noise for Raman spectroscopy
author: Bertens, Zhang, et al.
materials: •Power conditioner: ONEAC PCm750I, 220–240 V, 3.1 A, 50/60 Hz•Laser with wavelength 785 nm: Laser Model SM 785 nm purchased from Innovative Photonic Solutions; Output Power 50 mW; Bandwidth 9.73 GHz.•Laser with wavelength 671 nm: Laser model: Ignis 671, purchased from Laser quantum; Output Power 100 mW; Bandwidth 30 GHz.•Spectrometer: Model HPRM 2500, produced by River Diagnostics International BV. Specifications:○Spectral region coverage: 350 cm−1 - 1800 cm−1 with the 785 nm laser and ~2500 cm−1 - 4000 cm−1 with the 671 nm laser.○Spectral resolution: 2 cm−1 throughout the spectral region○Pinhole size: 25 µm○Back-illuminated deep-depletion CCD-camera: with 1024 × 128 pixels, air-cooled to −60 °C. Camera control software included.•Computer: HP Compaq 6200 Pro-Microtower with operation system WindowsⓇ 7 Pro-OA.•Jena lens: Planachromat LD 25x/0.5 ∞/0(2)-A, focus length is 10.1 mm.•Mirror: Beam steering mirror assembly, model G063713000.•Melles Griot Shear-plate•Fibres: DiamondⓇ FC APC/PM 20,853,190,002 for 850 nm and FC APC/PM 20,871,100,001 for 630 nm•GonioLens, Haag-Streit Meridian; CGA1•Edmund Optics lenses: f60 (60 mm focus point), f80 (80 mm focus point)

steps.title: Gather equipment and reagents
steps.instruction: Collect all hardware and software required for the Raman pipeline with the exact specifications listed in the Materials section.

substeps.instruction: Power conditioner: ONEAC PCm750I, 220–240 V, 3.1 A, 50/60 Hz.
785 nm laser: Model SM 785 nm (Innovative Photonic Solutions), output 50 mW, bandwidth 9.73 GHz.
671 nm laser: Model Ignis 671 (Laser Quantum), output 100 mW, bandwidth 30 GHz.

Spectrometer: Model HPRM 2500 (River Diagnostics International BV) – spectral region 350–1800 cm⁻¹ (785 nm) and ~2500–4000 cm⁻¹ (671 nm), resolution 2 cm⁻¹, pinhole 25 µm, back‑illuminated deep‑depletion CCD 1024 × 128 pixels cooled to –60 °C.
Computer: HP Compaq 6200 Pro‑Microtower, Windows 7 Pro‑OA.
Software: OriginPro 9.0.0 (64‑bit) and MATLAB 2017b.
Lenses: Jena Planachromat LD 25x/0.5 (focus length 10.1 mm), Edmund Optics f60 (60 mm focus) and f80 (80 mm focus).
Mirror: Beam steering mirror assembly, model G063713000.
Shear‑plate: Melles Griot shear‑plate.
Optical fibres: Diamond® FC APC/PM 20,853,190,002 for 850 nm and FC APC/PM 20,871,100,001 for 630 nm.
GonioLens (CGA1).
Methocel® 2% (topical application for eye measurements).

steps.title: Connect and power Raman system
steps.instruction: Hook the Raman instrument to the power conditioner, turn on the lasers and set their continuous output powers to the values used in the protocol.

substeps.instruction: Connect the power conditioner to the Raman system to protect against power peaks.
Turn on the 785 nm laser and set continuous power to 26 mW (despite the 50 mW maximum rating).
Turn on the 671 nm laser and set continuous power to 14 mW (despite the 100 mW maximum rating).
Ensure the spectrometer CCD is cooled to –60 °C.

steps.title: Align laser beam and collimate
steps.instruction: Guide the laser light through the diamond optical fibre, shape it with the 25 µm pinhole, and collimate the output using the f80 lens while verifying collimation with the shear‑plate.

substeps.instruction: Introduce the laser light into the diamond optical fibre.
Pass the beam through the 25 µm pinhole onto the measurement stage.
Place the converging f80 lens (Edmund Optics) in the beam path to collimate the emitted light.
Inspect the beam on the Melles Griot shear‑plate; move the lens along the laser axis until the shear‑plate stripes indicate a collimated beam.

steps.title: Prepare sample mounting configuration
steps.instruction: Select and assemble the appropriate front‑of‑sample optics for the type of sample being measured.

substeps.instruction: Cuvette set‑up: Position the f80 lens directly in front of the sample placed in a Brand® cuvette.
Jena lens set‑up: Position the long‑working‑distance Jena microscope objective (Planachromat LD 25x/0.5, 10.1 mm focal length) in front of the sample.
Gonio lens set‑up: Place the f60 lens followed by the Gonio lens (CGA1) in front of the eye; apply Methocel® 2% to the cornea for in‑vivo or ex‑vivo measurements.

steps.title: Calibrate spectrometer
steps.instruction: Perform the built‑in calibration of the spectrometer, then refine it with a NIST‑standard glass reference spectrum, following the instrument manual, and keep the measurement environment dark.

substeps.instruction: With the laser collimated and the measurement lens in place, run the spectrometer’s built‑in calibration routine.
Acquire a reference spectrum from the NIST‑standard calibration glass supplied with the spectrometer.
Complete the full calibration according to the HPRM 2500 manual.
Ensure all subsequent measurements are performed in a dark environment.

steps.title: Determine measurement position using 671 nm laser
steps.instruction: Activate the 671 nm laser, acquire a high‑wave‑number spectrum, and locate the desired region by identifying characteristic protein and water peaks.

substeps.instruction: Record the high‑wave‑number signal (2000–3800 cm⁻¹).
For eye measurements, recognize corneal protein peak (2800–3000 cm⁻¹) and water band (3000–3800 cm⁻¹); anterior chamber shows only water band; lens shows an additional protein peak around 3100 cm⁻¹.
For cuvette measurements, note multiple high‑intensity signals (2000–3000 cm⁻¹) when focusing on the cuvette wall and a water peak (3000–3800 cm⁻¹) when focusing on the fluid.
Adjust focus until the spectrum matches the target region’s peak pattern.

steps.title: Acquire Raman fingerprint spectrum
steps.instruction: Switch to the 785 nm laser, record the fingerprint region of the sample, and export the data as a text file.

substeps.instruction: Confirm the laser is correctly positioned based on the previous step.
Collect the Raman fingerprint spectrum with the 785 nm laser.
Export the spectrum as a ‘.txt’ file for downstream processing.

steps.title: Remove cosmic ray spikes in OriginPro
steps.instruction: Open each exported spectrum in OriginPro 9.0.0, manually inspect for cosmic‑ray spikes, and replace affected wavenumbers with values from another acquisition frame.

substeps.instruction: Load the .txt file into OriginPro 9.0.0 (64‑bit).
Inspect the spectrum visually for sharp, isolated intensity spikes.
For each spike, copy the intensity value from the same wavenumber in a different frame and overwrite the spike.
Save the corrected spectrum.

steps.title: Process spectra in MATLAB
steps.instruction: Import the cleaned spectra into MATLAB 2017b and apply the baseline‑removal pipeline (partial 5th‑degree polynomial fitting and top‑hat filtering) as described by Perez‑Pueyo et al. (2010).

substeps.instruction: Load the corrected .txt files into MATLAB 2017b.
Implement the partial 5th‑degree polynomial fit to model the baseline.
Apply top‑hat morphological filtering to eliminate hardware‑related artifacts.
Save the final processed spectra for analysis.
